classification.difficultyReason: Recognise connected acyclic networks, distinguishing curved edges from cycles and identifying a loop.

content.prompt: Identify which of the following are trees.

spec.description: Eight unlabelled vertices, two branching junctions and curved connections; no crossing or cycle.
spec.mathematics: Connected graph with eight vertices and seven edges; exactly one path between any two vertices.

answer.worked: It is connected and has no cycles, so there is exactly one path between any two vertices. Its 8 vertices are joined by 7 edges.

spec.description: Eight unlabelled vertices; an upper-left branch joins a curved connection followed by a chain to the upper-right endpoint.
spec.mathematics: Connected graph with eight vertices and seven edges, without a cycle.

answer.worked: It is connected and has no cycles, so there is exactly one path between any two vertices. Its 8 vertices are joined by 7 edges.

spec.description: Upper quadrilateral cycle with a right leaf and a descending three-edge branch at its lower junction.
spec.mathematics: Eight vertices and eight edges; the upper four vertices form a cycle.

answer.worked: The upper quadrilateral is a cycle. There is more than one path between vertices on that cycle, so the graph is not a tree.

spec.description: Central five-way junction with three left leaves and two branches through marked intermediate vertices to right leaves. Curves do not close into cycles.
spec.mathematics: Connected graph with eight vertices and seven edges; no loops, multiple edges or cycles.

answer.worked: It is connected and has no cycles. The curved edges do not form closed paths. Its 8 vertices are joined by 7 edges.

spec.description: Eight vertices on a branching network with a loop attached to the upper-right marked vertex.
spec.mathematics: Seven connecting edges plus one loop. A loop prevents the graph from being a tree.

answer.worked: The upper-right vertex has a loop. A tree has no loops.

spec.description: Upper junction with three upper leaves; upper junction, left-middle vertex and lower junction form a triangle. Lower junction has two further leaves.
spec.mathematics: Eight vertices and eight edges; the triangle is a cycle.

answer.worked: The two junctions and the left-middle vertex form a triangular cycle. A tree has no cycles.
